newsitem.title: UK: UK firms want tough gas transport price regime.
newsitem.headline: UK firms want tough gas transport price regime.

text.p: British companies on Thursday renewed their call for a tougher gas transport price regime than proposed by industry watchdog Ofgas.
The regulator's proposals are currently being vetted by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) after they were rejected in October by BG Plc, which said they were too harsh.
But the companies represented by the Energy Intensive Users Group believe the MMC should push for a price control which would be even tougher than that proposed by Ofgas.
"Industrial customers are horrified by the prospect of yet another compromise control," said the group's policy adviser, Lisa Waters.

The Energy Intensive Users Group said it wrote a letter to the MMC to underline its point. The MMC will report its findings to Ofgas by May 31, which is unlikely to make the results public before mid-July.
Ofgas proposed a one-off price cut by BG's pipeline operator TransCo of 20 percent. This would lead to an average reduction in domestic gas bills of about 30 stg per year, the regulator said.
BG said the proposals would lead to big job cuts, and would not allow it to maintain an efficient network.
